speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) how are potential grassroots leaders, key appointment holders and patrons vetted to ensure they are not susceptible to foreign influence; (b) whether there are regular review processes in place after appointment to identify and address potential vulnerabilities; (c) whether citizens born or educated outside Singapore are subject to more stringent vetting criteria; and (d) how are grassroots members empowered to critically evaluate information and resist undue foreign influence, especially from social media.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To achieve this, grassroots leaders, or GRLs, volunteer with PA, to help PA with its mission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: GRLs come from all walks of life, representing a diverse cross section of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They volunteer their time, effort and resources to serve Singaporeans and make Singapore a better home for all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: GRLs also help the Government communicate policies to residents and receive feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To fulfil this role, it is important that GRLs can discern information from misinformation and are able to critically evaluate information that they receive, including from social media sources.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: PA supports GRLs in this role by regularly sharing key information on Government policies, with regular dialogues, both formal as well as informal, held with GRLs on national and local issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This also includes open discussions at regular Grassroots Organisations (GRO) meetings so that GRLs better understand the intent of various Government initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, the National Community Leadership Institute, or NACLI, conducts workshops to equip GRLs with the knowledge and skills to identify and manage misinformation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Indeed, our GRLs in the community, play critical roles in community engagement and facilitating better Government to citizen communications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How often are the regular review processes conducted after GRLs are appointed and does this review include an assessment of the susceptibility to foreign influence?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, with the proliferation of social media a few years ago, we looked at that as an additional factor.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also look at the local ground conditions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: What are some of the organisations that the GROs partner with, in fulfilling their mission or conducting their events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The point, really, also is to not just focus on the systemic reviews and the processes that we look at regularly, but also to apply a common sense approach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When you assess an individual, when you get wind of, perhaps, a person becoming too close or unnaturally closer to one or more organisations, then, I think that you can surface it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Which segues into the second question on what are the avenues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are now grassroots' mentors that we appoint.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are senior, more experienced GRLs who have since retired from their position.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They are deployed in various constituencies and serve the constituency as a resource person and more from a mentor perspective, to cast a broader view with their experience.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And of course, there are also the grassroots' advisor and other organisations to whom you can raise any particular observations or concerns.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Do Permanent Residents (PRs) and foreigners participate in our grassroot activities and are any of them in leadership positions?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The short answer is PRs and non-citizens, they are welcome to take part in events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They make up a part of the Singaporean society, so they are present in the events.
